status: conditional retained-prefix algorithm comparison; neither representation adopted
value_lineage: C-29/P-69 incoming gather must identify the retained inputs to each target; C-13/P-26 provides bounded storage, while P-30 makes it available to learning. H-34/H-74 require those actual traversal/growth/migration needs before considering any additional structure.
requirements: Distinguish reserved capacity from retained edges for gather, adaptation, growth and migration.
Preserve a retained association even when its current weight is zero, unless a separately defined learning operation removes it.
Keep neuron identity and effective edge weights unchanged during representation-only reassignment; publish a complete row at the agreed boundary.

common_candidate.live_prefix: Retained endpoint/weight pairs occupy positions0..d-1 in the assigned fixed-capacity set; remaining positions are unused. This is a candidate organization, not an accepted layout.
common_candidate.zero_weight: Zero weight is not an empty marker: the endpoint can still identify an association eligible for later adaptation. Declaring it absent would change topology/learning semantics.
common_candidate.endpoint_namespace: At N=614400, a distinguished uint32 value outside valid intra-CC neuron IDs can mark a prefix end. No future endpoint namespace or particular sentinel code is fixed.
common_candidate.multiplicity: Under the one-retained-edge-per-source/target candidate, growth excludes already represented source IDs. Multiple contacts between the same endpoints would need separate semantics; duplicate checking is not solved by either prefix-end encoding.

candidates.name: Endpoint end marker with capacity bound
candidates.semantics: For d<capacity, endpoint[d] is a reserved invalid value. Stop before reading a weight or source state for it. At d=capacity, the capacity bound terminates the row without an extra marker slot.
candidates.storage: No additional persistent array; the marker occupies an already unused endpoint element. Slots beyond it are not graph members.
candidates.operations: Gather discovers d while visiting the row. An algorithm performing adaptation/growth at that visit may reuse d as temporary worker state. A later unrelated operation must rediscover it if no other information supplies it.
candidates.limits: Marker checking and bounded iteration have execution cost. This is not proven faster than a count, and using zero as the sentinel would conflict with a valid zero-based neuron ID unless the namespace explicitly excluded it.

candidates.name: Separate uint16 live count per neuron
candidates.semantics: The target count d bounds the retained prefix; capacity still comes from the assigned class. No endpoint end marker is needed.
candidates.operations: End lookup is direct; repeated operations can use it without rediscovering the end. Growth/removal must keep count and row contents consistent at publication. Pure migration with unchanged d need not change the logical count.
candidates.limits: The current maximum capacities12800/18432 fit uint16. This is a justified comparison candidate, not an addition to the accepted array budget. Separate SoA storage respects standard16-bit width; no bit packing into owner IDs is proposed.

traffic.symbols: E retained edges, N_a assigned targets, U underfilled assigned sets.
traffic.marker: 5*E+4*U logical ID/weight/stop-check bytes per row sweep.
traffic.count: 5*E+2*N_a logical ID/weight/count bytes per row sweep.
traffic.limit: Counts assume four-byte endpoints and one-byte weights, exactly one read of each named item, and the stated row loops. Reference loads, scattered source-state reads, decoding, arithmetic, cache-line transfers, prefetch, branches, writes and learning are additional. Logical bytes do not establish DRAM traffic, speed or Pi viability.

mutation_boundaries.append: Write new endpoint and weight before publishing the new logical end. For the marker candidate, initialize the next marker if capacity remains. A complete-frame boundary can serialize these operations without choosing new synchronization machinery.
mutation_boundaries.removal: No removal policy is selected. If one is justified, moving the last retained pair into a hole can preserve the mathematical edge multiset but changes reduction order. Preserving order uses different work; choose only after the numerical/behavioral requirement is established.
mutation_boundaries.migration: Copy the retained d pairs, then establish the destination end representation before publication. Five*d copied payload bytes imply about10*d source-read/destination-write bytes; an underfilled destination marker adds one4-byte write in that candidate, before reference/owner and cache costs.
mutation_boundaries.floating_order: Reordering retained pairs can change a floating-point sum despite unchanged real-valued graph semantics. Effective-weight preservation alone does not establish bit-identical responses; no determinism requirement or sorting scheme is selected.
mutation_boundaries.free_set_selection: The existing owner map indicates assignment. A prefix representation does not select free-set discovery/reservation, migration timing or a replacement rule.

decision_evidence: Favor an explicit count only if repeated end queries, useful vectorization or measured traversal/update cost justify its persistent state. Favor the marker if it supplies the required operations more simply at adequate cost. Compare the same retained graph, state precision and update schedule; no free list, row index, extra topology or runtime experiment is prescribed.
non_adoptions: No count array, sentinel code, prefix layout, pruning policy, sort, duplicate hash, free list or allocator implementation is selected.
No change to pool quotas, min-capacity admission, weight scale, five-byte slot payload or existing state-field choices.
No neural training, benchmark, project tests, build, toolchain change, commit or push.
